---
monokl: minor
---

`monokl search` rows now show the lines that matched, so you often don't need a second read of the file to see why a block matched.

- **New `snippet` column.** It sits after `symbolSignature` and holds the matching lines of the block, each with its line number and cut at 160 characters. Scripts that read rows by position must account for the extra column.
- **Bounded.** It shows up to three lines, then says how many more matched (`...and 2 more matching lines`). It is `null` when nothing beyond the signature matched.
- **No repeat of the signature.** A block with a signature leaves out its first line; a variable or type alias, which has no signature, shows it.

content.text:
The snippet feature is built, tested and pushed, but there's no GitHub PR for it yet. I created the trail through Entire as you asked. That published `feat/search-snippets`, and Entire made trail 254 with change #32, but it hasn't opened a GitHub PR so far. I checked twice and `gh pr list` shows none. I did not fall back to `gh pr create`. The Entire change is at https://entire.com/gh/orin-dx/-/trails/254/changes/monokl/32.

The change is stacked on #60 and adds a `snippet` column to every `monokl search` row. It shows the lines of the block that matched, numbered, at most three, each cut at 160 characters, with the rest counted ("...and 2 more matching lines").

- **Why:** before this, rows held only a location and a signature, so an agent had to read the file to see why a block matched.
- **Effect:** `just rg-compare` shows the declaration's own line in the output for 47 of 59 identifiers, up from 4 of 59. Output grew about 1.7x and stayed below one `rg -n` call (for example 37 KB against 61 KB on zod). The same run exits 0 at the 90% gate with 56 of 59 in the top 3.
- **Variable rows:** while checking the first output I caught that variables and type aliases, which have no signature, showed nothing. I fixed that test-first, so their first line is shown.
- **Checks I ran locally:**
  - 633 tests pass (up from 620).
  - `just lint` (now including `typos`), `doc-check`, `check-drift`, `machete` and `callisto status --check --strict` all pass.
  - `just coverage` reports 98.2% lines against the 90% gate.
  - CI on the PR has not run yet.
- **Docs:** I added a minor changeset, updated the README and recorded the decision as §26 in the decision log. The old test saying block code must never appear in rows assumed a separate `extract` command that was never built.

Open items:
- **Output budget:** `--max-tokens` and `--max-bytes` still count the blocks the rows cover, not the snippets printed. The gap is small, at most about 500 bytes a row.
- **Missing declarations:** 12 of the 59 declarations are still not in the output. I haven't diagnosed why.
- **Entire shadow PR:** I don't know whether Entire opens the GitHub PR on its own after a delay. If it doesn't appear soon, tell me how you create PRs from a trail and I'll do that.

**tsrs** is Oxc's experimental Rust port of the TypeScript type checker. It is not the same project as Ezno, another Rust checker that Oxc's forks also mention.

- **What it is:** The Oxc docs describe tsrs as a Rust port of the TypeScript compiler and language server, incubated within Oxc. Cloudflare, VoidZero, and Max Schwenk are developing it in collaboration with the TypeScript team.
- **Goals and status:** The docs say it aims for full TypeScript compatibility, but some differences remain. The goal is faster type checking and lower memory use while preserving upstream TypeScript behavior. Coverage is tracked in a compatibility document.
- **Usage:** You install it as a dev dependency (for example, npm add -D tsrs) and run npx tsrs --noEmit to check types without emitting JavaScript.
- **Performance claims:** Early figures are vendor-reported. One source cites up to 8× faster checking and roughly 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0 at equal checker counts, and notes that those are early vendor benchmarks, with results that depend on the workload.
- **Origin:** One article says the project was announced on October 20, 2026, and that it starts from Microsoft's Go-based compiler. It describes tsrs as a function-by-function port of the Go implementation.
- **Ezno (separate project):** The Oxc README lists Ezno as a different checker. Developed by @kaleidawave, ezno is a TypeScript checker written in Rust with a focus on static analysis and runtime performance.

Sources: the official Oxc docs (oxc.rs), a Flavio Copes deep dive, and a RuntimeWire article. The GitHub results I found were forks, so I relied on the docs for Oxc's own description.

content.text:
Yes, the oxc type checker (tsrs) could be useful to us later, but I wouldn't adopt it now, and most of what I know about it is secondhand.

**What it is.** Per [the oxc docs](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/typechecker), tsrs is an experimental Rust port of the TypeScript compiler, built with Cloudflare and VoidZero and developed with the TypeScript team. It is run with `npx tsrs --noEmit`. An [article on the announcement](https://runtimewire.com/article/cloudflare-tsrs-rust-typescript-compiler-wasm) gives a date of 20 October 2026 and calls it a function-by-function port of the Go compiler. The speed claims (up to 8x faster, about 70% less memory) are the vendors' own early figures. I have not run it, and I haven't confirmed whether it is a usable library or only a CLI.

**Why not now.**
- **The goal doesn't need it.** monokl's job is answering a question with a few ranked blocks, fast, in little context. That is lexical and structural, and the harness shows it works: the declaration is in the top 3 for 56 of 59 identifiers and its line is in the output for 59 of 59.
- **It costs the speed we want.** Type checking loads the whole program and its tsconfig. monokl is a fresh process of about 50 ms per search, and a checker belongs in the daemon-style design the spec already reserved for heavy analysis.
- **It makes monokl depend on an experimental tool.** The project's own non-goals avoid that kind of dependency.

**Where it would help.** A future "what is the type of X", "who implements this interface", or a precise reference/definition command would need real type information. Today those fall back to `rg`. The spec already plans an `oxc_semantic` upgrade for within-file scope-aware lookups, and tsrs would be the cross-file step after that.

**What I'd do.** Add it to the research notes as a watch item and revisit when we build a type-aware command. I won't add a dependency. Say if you want me to dig into the crate and API first.

**Other work this turn:**
- **Metric fix:** my "declaration in output" metric was wrong. It failed on the `export ` prefix and the trailing brace that signatures drop. With it fixed, the figure is 59 of 59 after the change and 15 of 59 before. I corrected the decision record and the trail.
- **Corrected figures:** those replace the 47 and 4 I gave earlier, and I measured the baseline with the same corrected metric.
- **Still pending:** no GitHub PR exists for `feat/search-snippets` yet, so CI hasn't run on it. Tell me how Entire opens the PR from a trail change.
Keep going on our work theb

EVAL DECISION: - Decision: score multi-word questions (2 to 4 words, known answer file and symbol) beside identifier lookups, gated on answer file in top 3 at a 75% default. Why: identifier lookups are where rg already wins on cost; baseline is 14/18, so 75% leaves one question of headroom.
- Decision: answers are recorded in scripts/rg-compare.questions and re-verified by rg against the pinned sha on every run. Why: a stale row fails loudly instead of silently scoring wrong.
- Rejected: model-judged relevance. Why: needs model calls, is non-deterministic, and the task rules them out.
- Open: raise the threshold when ranking improves. The 4 misses are zod 'json schema convert' (rank 8), zod 'safe parse result' (rank 5), axios 'build full path base url' (rank 5) and axios 'dispatch request adapter' (rank 4).
SUMMARY: DESIGN MEMO: member-level blocks

Recommendation: emit member blocks in the same analyzer pass, as additional CodeBlocks next to the top-level one, with the innermost block winning matched_lines.

What to extract (OXC kinds). Today `block()` runs once per top-level statement (parse.rs:364, called from `statement()` at :172). `statement_kind` (:399) is the only gate. Add a member walk inside `block()` for these kinds only:
- `ClassBody` elements `MethodDefinition` (Method, or Constructor when `kind == Constructor`) and `PropertyDefinition` whose value is an arrow function or function expression (Property).
- `ObjectExpression` properties in a top-level `const X = {...}`: `ObjectProperty` with an arrow/function value, or `method: true`.
- Hooks: a `VariableDeclaration` directly in the body of a component, meaning a top-level function or a const bound to an arrow function, where the init is a `CallExpression` whose callee name matches `use[A-Z]`. Emit only for `useCallback`, `useMemo` and `useEffect` bodies of at least 5 lines. This is the noisiest category, so it goes in the last PR.
- Skip members of fewer than 3 lines, and skip interface and type members.

SymbolKind already has Method, Constructor, Property (boost.rs:55-57), so no new variants are needed.

Nesting, dedup and matched_lines.
- `retrieve_blocks` (pipeline/mod.rs:269) assigns by range containment at :300-301. A nested member's lines would be matched by both parent and child, so a match counts twice.
- Fix: compute the innermost block per hit (smallest enclosing range) and strip those lines from the ancestors' `matched_lines`. An ancestor with no remaining direct lines is dropped, unless it matches on its own header line. This keeps "class named Foo matches Foo" and prevents the class from also winning on a method body.
- `dedup_blocks` (dedup.rs:41,63) drops any later block whose overlap is more than half of the smaller block. A member is always fully inside its parent, so overlap is 100% and the lower-ranked one is dropped. That is the desired behavior when the parent ranks higher, but it makes members vanish whenever the class outranks them.
- Fix: exempt strict parent/child containment from `overlaps_significantly`. Instead, when the parent has no direct matched lines, drop the parent (see above).

Ranking. `node_type_boost` (boost.rs:50) gives Method/Constructor 1.4 and Property 1.0, which is already below Function 1.5 and Class 1.4. BM25 doc length (rank/mod.rs:73-76) favors short members for free. Leave the boost table alone. Make no change to scoring in PR 1.

Output. `RankedBlock.parent_context` and `ParentContext{kind,name,line}` already exist (types.rs:157,172) but are always None (rank/mod.rs:82). Populate it from the extraction. Add `parent` as a 9th TOON column after `nodeKind` (agent.rs:171). Encode it as `Class Foo`, or omit it for top-level blocks. `symbolSignature` stays the member's own signature.

Output size. The row count is unchanged because of `--limit`. Each member row is smaller than the class it replaces. The cost is one new column, roughly 6 tokens on member rows only. Whole-class rows disappear when only one method matched.

Tests that pin it (assert exact values):
1. Fixture class with two methods, query on one method name: exactly one row, a Method, with the parent `Class Foo`.
2. The class header match still returns the Class row.
3. A line is never in two blocks' `matched_lines`.
4. dedup keeps a child with a parent present, per the new containment rule.
5. An object-literal property function and a hook each get a row.
6. A proptest on innermost assignment.
7. A snapshot of the TOON header.
8. Update the empty-result hint at output/agent.rs:201 and its test at :436.

Risks. Fixture and snapshot churn. Hook false positives. Block count growth slows BM25 corpus stats (`corpus_size` at rank/mod.rs:70 counts nested blocks, so IDF shifts). The nested blocks duplicate parent text in memory.

Order of PRs.
1. Class methods and constructors: extraction, innermost assignment, dedup containment rule, parent column, hint text.
2. Object-literal property functions and class property arrow functions (reuses the same machinery).
3. Hooks inside components, behind the size threshold, plus a tuning test.

Alternative rejected: keep top-level blocks only and make the output show the enclosing block's matched lines as a better snippet (already shipped in e82cf84). Rejected because the row still names and ranks the whole class, so a member name query cannot rank the member above its siblings, and the BM25 length penalty hits large classes.

Not executed: no cargo run, nothing tested. The OXC node kind names (MethodDefinition, PropertyDefinition, ObjectProperty) are from my knowledge and were not checked against the oxc version in Cargo.lock.

All four tracks are done. Three PRs are ready for review, and the speed investigation found the cause but made no fix.

**The 40 ms cost is the tokenizer, not the pipeline.** The first token count builds tiktoken's `o200k` vocabulary, which took about 55 ms. Text search, parsing and ranking add about 3 ms in total. A search that matches nothing never counts tokens, which is why it stays near 6 ms. The perf agent made no change because the code is in `budget.rs`, which another track owned.

I recommend replacing tiktoken with a plain byte-based estimate, such as bytes divided by 4. That drops the 55 ms, the dependency, and the vocabulary data in the binary. `o200k` is OpenAI's tokenizer, so it isn't exact for whatever model reads the output anyway. It's your call, since it changes what `--max-tokens` means slightly.

**PRs.** Entire opened them as drafts, and I marked them ready. #62 and #61 are stacked on #63, so merge #63 first.

| PR | What | State |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #63 | `snippet` column (retargeted to main after #60 merged) | Lint, MSRV, Audit and Changesets pass; macOS Test, Coverage and Entire Gates still pending |
| #62 | `--max-tokens` and `--max-bytes` count the printed row text, not block code | Same state |
| #61 | 18 multi-word questions, 6 per repo, scored against rg | Not checked yet |

- **#62 (budget caps):** the agent wrote the new CLI tests after the code and did not see them fail first, so the guarantee is weaker than usual. Defaults stay at 50 results, 20,000 tokens and 2 MiB, because the worst output measured was 11 KB. It reports 639 tests and 98.16% coverage.
- **#61 (question eval):** for 14 of the 18 questions the answer file is in the top 3, and the new gate is 75%. The four misses are rank 4 to 8, and I haven't diagnosed them.

**Design memo, member-level blocks.** The agent recommends emitting method, constructor and property blocks beside the top-level one, with the innermost block winning the matched lines. A ninth `parent` column would carry context such as `Class Foo`, and the dedup rule would stop treating a member inside its parent as an overlap. It proposes three PRs: class methods first, then object-literal and class-property functions, then hooks. Its OXC node names are from memory and not checked against our version. I'd start with PR 1 after the budget work.

**Housekeeping:**
- **Trail 254 / #63:** I retargeted it with `entire trail link 254 --base main`, and Entire then opened the PR.
- **Decision-log text:** I still need to merge the agents' decision-log text into the spec log. I'll do that when #63 merges, to avoid conflicts.

**Next:** unless you object, I'll have an agent replace tiktoken with the estimate, on its own branch, once #62 merges, since both change `budget.rs`.

---
monokl: patch

`monokl search` is faster whenever it finds a match, about 50 ms faster on a small repository, because it no longer loads a tokenizer vocabulary before printing.

- **`--max-tokens` is an estimate.** It counts one token per three bytes of the printed rows, rounded up, which reads about a tenth above `o200k_base` on real output. The default of 20,000 is unchanged.
- **Smaller install.** The tokenizer and its vocabulary are no longer part of the binary.

'- **Why.** Building the `o200k_base` vocabulary took about 55 ms on the first row of any search with a match, against about 6 ms for the rest of the search: a match cost 50 ms where `rg` costs 9 (zustand, release build). On 15 real outputs from the pinned repos `o200k_base` ran 2.97 to 3.57 bytes per token (mean 3.34), so `ceil(bytes / 3)` reads about 11% high on average and never more than 1% low. The cap is a backstop: the worst output measured was 11 KB, about 3,000 tokens, and `--max-results` usually binds first. No vocabulary is the one every reader uses, so the exact count was exact for the wrong tokenizer.' '- **Also removed.** The 32 KiB byte cap that kept quadratic BPE merging away from minified rows has no purpose without a tokenizer.' '- **Rejected.** Keeping the tokenizer and building it on a thread while text search runs: it hides the cost on large repositories only, keeps the dependency and the binary size, and keeps counting with the wrong vocabulary. Rejected: `bytes / 4`, which reads about 17% low on these outputs and so lets a response overspend its cap.' '- **Supersedes.** Part 8 §9.1 (byte length as a proven upper bound on tokens) still holds as a bound; the count now uses a tighter ratio and gives up the guarantee that it never understates.' >> docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md

content.text:
There are no open findings, and the tokenizer fix is up as PR #64, ready for review. CI on #64 is still pending.

**Findings**
- I checked every monokl change on trails 254 and newer. All report zero open findings.
- The one finding from earlier, on the `--no-questions` gate in change 35, was real, and I fixed it (4669e2d) and resolved it. It is on main, since #63 merged with the fix. After the merge the CLI shows zero resolved because it refuses findings on merged changes.
- #59, the release PR, has no findings either. Its gate fails only on "no reviewers have approved this trail". Approving the release is your call, so I left it.

**Speed fix (#64)**
- **Cost removed:** the 40 ms came from building tiktoken's `o200k` vocabulary on the first token count. That is now replaced by an estimate of one token per three bytes, and the dependency is removed.
- **Timing:** on zustand a match went from about 49 ms to 9 to 11 ms, level with `rg -l` in the same run (10.9 ms). A search with no match was already fast.
- **Estimate accuracy:** over 15 real outputs `o200k` ran 2.97 to 3.57 bytes per token (mean 3.34). The estimate therefore reads about 11% high on average and never more than 1% low. I rejected `bytes / 4` because it reads about 17% low and would let a response overspend its cap.
- **Behavior check:** the same 15 queries print byte-identical output. 637 tests pass, coverage is 98.14%, and lint, `typos`, doc-check, deny, machete, drift and changesets pass locally. I added a patch changeset and a decision-log entry (§27). The CLI help and README now say `--max-tokens` is an estimate.
- **Caveat:** the default of 20,000 tokens is unchanged, but the cap now bites at slightly different row counts than before. In practice `--max-results` binds first (worst measured output was about 3,000 tokens).

**Next:** member-level blocks, starting with the design memo's first PR (class methods and constructors, the innermost-block rule, and the `parent` column). That is the largest remaining gap for hit-first search, and the four missed eval questions are the best test of it.
Continue promptly and using agent teams and workflows for comprehensive implementation with maximum effort and being mindful of context/token usage when picking models and effort

Member-level blocks is the biggest change left, so I'm running it as a staged workflow. Parallel agents only on disjoint files, and effort scaled to the job.

| Stage | Agent | Files owned | Effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1a | implementer | `analysis/`, `pipeline/`, `rank/`, `output/`, tests, README, changeset | xhigh |
| 1b | eval questions | `scripts/` only | medium |
| 2 | adversarial reviewer (read-only, must reproduce) | none | high |
| 3 | fixer, only if confirmed findings | the implementer's branch | high |
